Diagnostics of an INLAvanilla fit

Source: R/diagnostics.R
diagnostics.Rd

The checks of each stage of the approximation, as numbers: a summary of the whole fit, or a table with one row per parameter. They are the checks of INLAvaan's diagnostics(), under the same names and in the same order, followed by inlavanilla's own. The fit-time warning and the flags of summary.inla_vanilla() are computed from the same numbers, and summary.inla_vanilla() explains each check and the level at which it is flagged.

Jamil and Rue (2026) use the VB shift and NMAD as fit diagnostics (Sections 3.1 and 4.4), and the gap between the skew-normal and VB means (mean_gap) as an internal check (Section 5.1). The mode shift, the Hessian condition number and the unscanned mass come from INLAvaan's diagnostics(), not from the paper. vb_step_sigma, tails and ridge_bend are inlavanilla's own.

Usage

diagnostics(object, ...)

# Default S3 method
diagnostics(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'inla_vanilla'
diagnostics(object, type = c("global", "param"), ...)

Arguments

object

An object of class inla_vanilla.

...

Unused.

type

"global" (the default) for the diagnostics of the whole fit, or "param" for those of each parameter.

Value

For type = "global", a named numeric vector of class inla_vanilla_diagnostics. For type = "param", a data frame of class inla_vanilla_diagnostics_param. Their print() methods use INLAvaan's formats.

Details

A posterior SD here is the Laplace SD at the mode, \(s_j = \sqrt{\Sigma_{jj}}\), as in INLAvaan; it is not the SD column of the summary table, which is the skew-normal's. Values that a fit did not compute are NA: the VB quantities with vb = FALSE, and the scan quantities with marginals = "gaussian".

Global diagnostics (type = "global"), a named numeric vector:

  • npar: the number of parameters.

  • converged: 1 if stats::nlminb() reported convergence (return code 0), 0 otherwise, as INLAvaan defines it. No check uses it: without a gradient nlminb() can report false convergence at an accurate mode. mode_shift_max checks the mode instead.

  • iterations: the iterations of nlminb(), in the run that was kept if it was restarted.

  • grad_inf, grad_inf_rel, grad_l2: the largest absolute value, the largest relative value and the Euclidean norm of grad (see below). They depend on the scale of each parameter.

  • mode_shift_max: the largest mode_shift_sigma. Unlike the gradient norms it is scale-free. It should be close to 0.

  • hess_cond: the condition number of the Hessian at the mode, with each parameter in its own posterior-SD units: the ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue of the posterior correlation matrix. Large values mean that some combination of the parameters is weakly identified. INLAvaan takes it on the raw scale of the parameters, where a mere change of units makes it large, so the two agree only when the posterior SDs are similar.

  • vb_applied: 1 if the VB correction ran, 0 otherwise.

  • vb_shift_max: the largest absolute vb_shift_sigma.

  • vb_kld_global: the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the Laplace Gaussian and its VB-shifted copy, \(\frac12 \delta^\top H \delta\), which is also the VB term of the log marginal likelihood.

  • kld_max, kld_mean: the largest and the mean kld.

  • nmad_max, nmad_mean: the largest and the mean nmad.

  • unscanned_mass_max: the largest unscanned_mass.

and then inlavanilla's own:

  • vb_fallback: 1 if the VB fixed-point iteration handed over to the fallback optimiser, 0 otherwise. Like INLAvaan, inlavanilla records it but flags nothing: the fallback is a route of the solver, not a measure of the approximation.

  • vb_step_max: the largest vb_step_sigma. Like mode_shift_max it should be close to 0.

  • mean_gap_max: the largest absolute mean_gap.

  • ridge_bend_max: the largest ridge_bend.

  • n_heavy_tails: the number of parameters whose tails is FALSE.

Per-parameter diagnostics (type = "param"), a data frame:

  • names: the parameter.

  • grad: the gradient of minus the log-posterior at the mode, as INLAvaan reports it: from grad when the fit has one, and otherwise from central differences of logpost a thousandth of a posterior SD apart. It should be close to 0.

  • grad_abs: its absolute value.

  • grad_rel: grad_abs / (abs(par) + 1e-6), with par the VB mean (the mode when vb = FALSE), as in INLAvaan.

  • mode_shift_sigma: the Newton step at the mode, in posterior SDs, \(|(\Sigma g)_j| / s_j\) with \(g\) the gradient. It should be close to 0.

  • kld: the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the Laplace Gaussian marginal and its VB-shifted copy, \(\delta_j^2 / (2\Sigma_{jj})\) = vb_shift_sigma^2 / 2. It is a function of the VB shift alone, and says nothing about the skew-normal fit.

  • vb_shift: the VB shift of the mean, \(\delta_j\), the VB mean minus the mode, on the scale of logpost.

  • vb_shift_sigma: the same in posterior SDs.

  • nmad: the NMAD of the skew-normal fit.

  • alpha: the shape of the fitted skew-normal marginal.

  • unscanned_mass: the mass the fitted skew-normal puts beyond the scanned window.

and then inlavanilla's own:

  • vb_step_sigma: the step still to go at the VB mean, in posterior SDs: the fixed-point step there, the Newton step of the VB stationarity condition, as mode_shift_sigma is for the mode. After the fallback optimiser it is taken where the optimiser landed. On the fixed-point path it is the last step taken, which bounds the next, unless that step was 0.1 or more (a vb_tol above 0.1), when it is taken afresh. It should be close to 0 (Inf where the step is not finite).

  • mean_gap, gamma1, tails and ridge_bend, which summary.inla_vanilla() describes.

Some of INLAvaan's diagnostics are left out. nsamp counts posterior draws, which sampling() makes on demand rather than during the fit. grad_num and grad_diff compare an analytic gradient with finite differences at the mode, which would take further calls; a supplied grad is checked at init and through the symmetry of its Jacobian at the mode instead, with a warning if either check fails. vb_mcse_max, vb_mcse_mean and vb_mcse_sigma estimate the quadrature error of INLAvaan's Sobol points, and the cubature rule of inlavanilla is deterministic (INLAvaan gives NA for its own deterministic rule).

INLAvaan also exports a diagnostics() generic, an S4 one. When both packages are attached, the one attached last masks the other. With inlavanilla attached last, its diagnostics() passes an INLAvaan fit on to INLAvaan's. With INLAvaan attached last, call inlavanilla::diagnostics(fit) for an inlavanilla fit.

References

Jamil, H., & Rue, H. (2026). Approximate Bayesian inference for structural equation models using integrated nested Laplace approximations (arXiv:2603.25690 [stat.ME]). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2603.25690

See also

summary.inla_vanilla() for what each check means and when it is flagged, and plot.inla_vanilla() with type = "sn_fit" for the skew-normal fits themselves.

Examples

set.seed(1)
y <- rnorm(30, mean = 5, sd = 2)
logpost <- function(theta, y) {
  sum(dnorm(y, theta[["mu"]], exp(theta[["log_sigma"]]), log = TRUE)) +
    dnorm(theta[["mu"]], 0, 10, log = TRUE) +
    dnorm(theta[["log_sigma"]], 0, 2, log = TRUE)
}
fit <- inla_vanilla(logpost, c(mu = 0, log_sigma = 0), y = y, silent = TRUE)

# The whole fit
diagnostics(fit)
#>               npar          converged         iterations           grad_inf 
#>                  2                  1                 10           1.96e-05 
#>       grad_inf_rel            grad_l2     mode_shift_max          hess_cond 
#>           3.13e-05           2.05e-05           2.53e-06           1.01e+00 
#>         vb_applied       vb_shift_max      vb_kld_global            kld_max 
#>                  1             0.2510             0.0315             0.0315 
#>           kld_mean           nmad_max          nmad_mean unscanned_mass_max 
#>             0.0158             0.0077             0.0039           6.58e-04 
#>        vb_fallback        vb_step_max       mean_gap_max     ridge_bend_max 
#>                  0           2.64e-04             0.0124             0.1324 
#>      n_heavy_tails 
#>                  0 

# One row per parameter
diagnostics(fit, type = "param")
#>       names grad grad_abs grad_rel mode_shift_sigma    kld vb_shift
#> 1        mu    0        0        0                0 0.0000  -0.0006
#> 2 log_sigma    0        0        0                0 0.0315   0.0323
#>   vb_shift_sigma   nmad   alpha unscanned_mass vb_step_sigma mean_gap
#> 1        -0.0017 0.0000 -0.2519       6.36e-05         0e+00  -0.0002
#> 2         0.2510 0.0077  1.3709       6.58e-04         3e-04   0.0124
#>    gamma1 tails ridge_bend
#> 1 -0.0002  TRUE     0.1324
#> 2  0.1282  TRUE     0.0000
